"Inject the PetrolEngine Bean specifically."

The qualifier value must match the bean name — by default, Spring uses the class name with a lowercase first letter as the bean name: PetrolEngine → "petrolEngine"

Complete Example

Engine Interface

Java
public interface Engine {
    void start();
}

Two Implementations

Java
@Component
public class PetrolEngine implements Engine {
    public void start() {
        System.out.println("Petrol Engine Started");
    }
}

@Component
public class DieselEngine implements Engine {
    public void start() {
        System.out.println("Diesel Engine Started");
    }
}

Car.java — With @Qualifier

Java
@Component
public class Car {

    @Autowired
    @Qualifier("petrolEngine")
    private Engine engine;

    public void drive() {
        engine.start();
        System.out.println("Car is running");
    }
}
ℹ️ Output
Petrol Engine Started
Car is running

Real-Life Analogy — Notebook Shop

Notebook Analogy
Imagine you order: "Bring me a notebook."

The shop has: Classmate Notebook · Navneet Notebook.

The shopkeeper asks: "Which one?"
You answer: "Navneet."
Real LifeSpring
NotebookBean type (Engine)
Navneet / ClassmateSpecific Bean (petrolEngine)
"Bring me Navneet"@Qualifier("petrolEngine")

Advantages

Resolves Bean ambiguity Precise control over dependency injection Prevents NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException Useful when multiple implementations exist
Module 5 · Spring AOP · 5f · i

Introduction to Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP)

A programming paradigm that separates common functionalities (cross-cutting concerns) from the main business logic — write once, apply everywhere.

What is AOP?

  • Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP) is a programming paradigm that separates common functionalities (cross-cutting concerns) from the main business logic.
  • With AOP, you write common code once, and Spring automatically applies it wherever needed.

Example — Online Banking Application

Suppose you're building an Online Banking Application with methods like: Transfer Money · Check Balance · Deposit Money · Withdraw Money.

Before every operation, you also want to:

Log the request Check user authentication Check authorization Measure execution time
❌

Without AOP

Java — Repeated Code
public void transferMoney() {
    // Logging
    // Security Check
    // Business Logic
}
public void withdrawMoney() {
    // Logging
    // Security Check
    // Business Logic
}
public void depositMoney() {
    // Logging
    // Security Check
    // Business Logic
}

Logging and Security code is repeated everywhere.

✅

With AOP

Write Logging and Security only once. Spring automatically applies them to every method where required.

Problem Without AOP

Diagram — Code Duplication
Transfer()
│
├── Logging
├── Security
└── Business Logic

Withdraw()
│
├── Logging
├── Security
└── Business Logic

Deposit()
│
├── Logging
├── Security
└── Business Logic
Code duplication Hard maintenance Difficult debugging Changes required in many places

Solution With AOP

Diagram — AOP Separation
                Logging
                   │
                   ▼
Transfer()    Business Logic

Withdraw()    Business Logic

Deposit()     Business Logic

                   ▲
                   │
               Security
💡 Key Insight
Logging and Security are now separate from business logic. Spring applies them automatically. The business methods only contain their core logic — clean and focused.

What is a Cross-Cutting Concern?

A Cross-Cutting Concern is a functionality that is used across multiple parts of an application.

Cross-Cutting ConcernDescription
LoggingRecord application activity
SecurityAuthentication & Authorization
Transaction ManagementCommit / Rollback database changes
Exception HandlingHandle errors centrally
Performance MonitoringMeasure execution time
CachingImprove performance

Advantages

Eliminates duplicate code Improves code readability Better separation of concerns Easier maintenance Reusable common functionalities Cleaner business logic
Module 5 · Spring AOP · 5f · ii

Creating Aspects and Advice

An Aspect is where common code lives. Advice is when that common code runs — the two core concepts that make AOP work in Spring.

What is an Aspect?

  • An Aspect is a class that contains cross-cutting concerns like logging, security, or transaction management.
  • Instead of writing logging inside every service method, you create one separate class — that class is called an Aspect.
ℹ️ Simple Formula
Aspect = Where the common code is written.
Banking Example
Suppose you have a BankService and you want Logging for every method. Instead of writing Logging inside every service method, create one separate class: LoggingAspect.

That class contains all logging logic — that's the Aspect.

Creating an Aspect

Spring provides @Aspect to mark a class as an Aspect:

Java — LoggingAspect.java
@Aspect
@Component
public class LoggingAspect {
    // All logging/cross-cutting logic goes here
}

Real-Life Analogy — Movie Theater

Movie Theater
Before the movie starts → Advertisement is shown.
Movie plays.
After the movie ends → Feedback is collected.
Movie TheaterSpring AOP
AdvertisementBefore Advice
MovieBusiness Method
FeedbackAfter Advice
Theater ManagerAspect

What is Advice?

  • Advice is the action performed by an Aspect at a specific time.
  • Examples: Before method execution · After method execution · Around method execution.
ℹ️ Simple Formula
Advice = When that common code executes.
Advice tells Spring when to execute the code.

Five Types of Advice

🔖 1) @Before — Runs Before method execution
Java
@Before("execution(* com.demo.*.*(..))")
public void log() {
    System.out.println("Logging Before Method");
}
🔖 2) @After — Runs After method execution (success or exception)
Java
@After("execution(* com.demo.*.*(..))")
public void log() {
    System.out.println("Logging After Method");
}
✅ 3) @AfterReturning — Runs After successful execution
Java
@AfterReturning("execution(* com.demo.*.*(..))")
public void success() {
    System.out.println("Method Executed Successfully");
}
⚠️ 4) @AfterThrowing — Runs After an exception occurs
Java
@AfterThrowing("execution(* com.demo.*.*(..))")
public void error() {
    System.out.println("Exception Occurred");
}
ℹ️ 5) @Around — Runs Before AND After the method
Java
@Around("execution(* com.demo.*.*(..))")
public Object execute(ProceedingJoinPoint pjp) throws Throwable {
    System.out.println("Before Method");
    Object result = pjp.proceed();  // Execute the actual method
    System.out.println("After Method");
    return result;
}

All 5 Advice Types — Summary

AdviceWhen It RunsUse Case
@BeforeBefore method executionLogging, Security check
@AfterAfter method (always)Cleanup, Audit trail
@AfterReturningAfter successful executionLog success result
@AfterThrowingAfter exception occursError logging, Alerts
@AroundBefore + AfterPerformance monitoring, Transactions

Advantages

Removes duplicate code Better separation of concerns Easier maintenance Centralized logging and security Cleaner business logic
Module 5 · Spring AOP · 5f · iii

Pointcuts and Joinpoints

A Joinpoint is every possible place where Advice can run. A Pointcut is the rule that selects exactly which ones it actually runs on.

What is a Join Point?

  • A Join Point is a point during program execution where Spring AOP can apply Advice.
  • In Spring AOP, every method execution is a Join Point.

Examples of Join Points

Method execution Exception handling Field access Object creation

Application Methods — All are Join Points

Application
Application
    │
    ├── login()             ← Join Point
    ├── register()          ← Join Point
    ├── transferMoney()     ← Join Point
    ├── withdrawMoney()     ← Join Point
    └── logout()            ← Join Point

Every method is a possible place where Spring can
run Logging, Security, etc. = Join Point
ℹ️ Simple Formula
Join Point = Every possible place where Advice can be applied.

What is a Pointcut?

  • A Pointcut is an expression (rule) that selects which Join Points should execute the Advice.
  • You don't want Advice on every single method — a Pointcut lets you target only the ones you need.
ℹ️ Simple Formula
Pointcut = The filter that selects which Join Points receive Advice.

Example — Select Only Specific Methods

Imagine you have 100 methods. You only want Logging for transferMoney() and withdrawMoney().

Pointcut Selection
Application
    │
    ├── login()              ✗ Not Selected
    ├── register()           ✗ Not Selected
    ├── transferMoney()      ✅ Selected
    ├── withdrawMoney()      ✅ Selected
    └── logout()             ✗ Not Selected

Only selected methods receive the Advice.

Pointcut Expression Syntax

Java — Pointcut Examples
// Apply to ALL methods in com.demo package
@Before("execution(* com.demo.*.*(..))")

// Apply only to transferMoney method
@Before("execution(* com.demo.BankService.transferMoney(..))")

// Apply to all methods in BankService
@Before("execution(* com.demo.BankService.*(..))")

Understanding the Execution Expression

PartMeaning
executionMatches method execution join points
* (return type)Any return type
com.demo.*Any class in com.demo package
.* (method)Any method name
(..)Any parameters (zero or more)

Full AOP Flow — Join Point → Pointcut → Advice

Application Methods (All are Join Points)
↓
Pointcut — Selects specific methods
↓
Advice — Logging / Security code runs
↓
Business Method Executes

Join Point vs Pointcut — Summary

ConceptDefinitionAnalogy
Join Point Every possible place where Advice can be applied (all methods) Every student in a school
Pointcut Expression that selects which Join Points to apply Advice to Only students in Class 10

Advantages

Fine-grained control over where Advice executes Avoids unnecessary Advice execution Improves performance by targeting only required methods Keeps AOP configuration organized
Module 5 · Spring AOP · 5f · iv

AOP Proxying Mechanisms

How Spring secretly wraps your beans in a Proxy to intercept method calls and apply Advice — without you changing a single line of business code.

What is a Proxy?

  • A Proxy is an object that acts as a middleman between the client and the real object.
  • Spring creates a Proxy around your bean to intercept method calls and apply Advice automatically.
❌

Without Spring AOP

Flow
User
 ↓
BankService
(Direct call — no interception)
✅

With Spring AOP — Proxy

Flow
User
 ↓
Proxy (intercepts)
 ↓
BankService
(Advice runs automatically)

Why Do We Need a Proxy?

Suppose you have transferMoney(). You never wrote logging(); inside it — yet Logging happens automatically.

ℹ️ How?
Spring creates a Proxy around the bean. The Proxy adds Logging automatically before calling the real method — without touching the original business code.
Spring Internal
Proxy
  ↓
transferMoney()  ← real method runs after Proxy applies Advice

Real-Life Analogy — Company Receptionist

CEO & Receptionist
Visitors never enter the CEO's office directly. They first meet the receptionist.

Visitor → Receptionist → CEO

The receptionist: checks identity · records visitor details · gives permission.
Only then can the visitor meet the CEO.
Real LifeSpring AOP
VisitorClient (calling code)
ReceptionistProxy
CEOTarget Object (BankService)
Identity CheckAdvice (Logging / Security)

What Does the Proxy Do?

When the client calls transferMoney(), the Proxy performs:

Client calls transferMoney()
↓
Proxy intercepts the call
↓
Logging runs (@Before Advice)
↓
Security check runs
↓
Real transferMoney() executes
↓
Result returned to client
💡 Key Insight
Everything happens automatically. The BankService class never knows a Proxy exists. The business code stays clean — no logging, no security code mixed in.

Advantages

Business classes remain clean Advice added without modifying original code Easy to add Logging, Security, Transactions Flexible and reusable
Module 5 · Spring AOP · 5f · v

Integrating AOP with Spring Applications

A complete working example — enabling AOP support with @EnableAspectJAutoProxy and wiring a LoggingAspect to run automatically with your business methods.

What is AOP Integration?

Integrating AOP with Spring means configuring Spring so that Aspects automatically execute along with your application's business methods.

⚠️ Simply Creating an Aspect Is Not Enough
Spring must know:
· Which class is an Aspect?
· Which methods contain Advice?
· When should Advice execute?

To do this, we enable AOP support in Spring.

Why @EnableAspectJAutoProxy?

Suppose you write:

Java
@Aspect
public class LoggingAspect {
}

Will Spring automatically execute it? No.

Spring must first be told: "Enable AOP support." That's why we use:

Java
@EnableAspectJAutoProxy

Complete Example

a) Business Class — BankService.java

Java
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

@Component
public class BankService {
    public void transferMoney() {
        System.out.println("Money Transferred");
    }
}

b) Aspect Class — LoggingAspect.java

Java
import org.aspectj.lang.annotation.Aspect;
import org.aspectj.lang.annotation.Before;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

@Aspect         // Marks this class as an Aspect
@Component      // Registers it as a Spring Bean
public class LoggingAspect {

    // Executes before transferMoney()
    @Before("execution(* transferMoney(..))")
    public void log() {
        System.out.println("Logging Before Transfer");
    }
}

c) Configuration Class — AppConfig.java

Java
import org.springframework.context.annotation.ComponentScan;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.EnableAspectJAutoProxy;

@Configuration              // Java Configuration class
@ComponentScan("com.demo") // Scan Spring Beans
@EnableAspectJAutoProxy     // Enable Spring AOP
public class AppConfig {

}

d) Main Class — Main.java

Java
import org.springframework.context.ApplicationContext;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.AnnotationConfigApplicationContext;

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {

        // Create Spring IoC Container
        ApplicationContext context =
            new AnnotationConfigApplicationContext(AppConfig.class);

        // Get BankService Bean
        BankService bankService = context.getBean(BankService.class);

        // Call business method
        bankService.transferMoney();
    }
}
ℹ️ Output
Logging Before Transfer
Money Transferred
💡 Notice
You never called log(); anywhere in your code. Spring automatically executed it — that's the power of AOP integration.

Key Annotations Used

AnnotationUsed OnPurpose
@AspectAspect classMarks the class as containing cross-cutting logic
@ComponentAspect classRegisters it as a Spring Bean so it's detected
@BeforeAdvice methodRuns before the matched method
@EnableAspectJAutoProxyConfig classTells Spring to enable AOP proxy support
@ComponentScanConfig classScans the package for beans and aspects

Advantages

Easy integration with Spring No changes to business classes Centralized logging and security Better code reuse Cleaner architecture
Module 5 · Spring MVC & ORM · 5g · i

Overview of MVC and ORM

MVC separates your application into Model, View, and Controller. ORM bridges Java objects and database tables — together they form the backbone of modern Spring web applications.

What is MVC?

  • MVC (Model-View-Controller) is a software design pattern that separates an application into three independent components: Model · View · Controller.
  • Instead of writing everything in one class, Spring divides the work across these three layers.

Beginner-Friendly Explanation — Amazon

Amazon Shopping Website
When you click "Search Product", many things happen behind the scenes. Spring MVC divides the work so each layer handles its own responsibility:
User sends request
↓
Controller — Receives the request
↓
Model — Fetches data / Business Logic
↓
Database
↓
View — Displays result to User
↓
User sees the result

Components of MVC

📦

a) Model

Responsible for: Data · Business Logic · Database communication.

Examples: Student · Employee · Product

🖥️

b) View

Responsible for: Showing information to the user.

Examples: Login Page · Home Page · Student List

🎮

c) Controller

Responsible for: Receiving requests · Calling Model · Returning View.

Examples: LoginController · StudentController · ProductController

Advantages of MVC

Better code organization Easy maintenance Easier debugging Reusable code Team members can work independently Clear separation of responsibilities

What is ORM?

  • ORM (Object Relational Mapping) is a technique that maps Java Objects to Database Tables.
☕

Java Understands

Student student;

Objects, classes, and references.

🗄️

Database Understands

STUDENT TABLE

Rows, columns, and SQL.

ℹ️ ORM connects both worlds.
It acts as a translator between Java objects and database tables.

Why Do We Need ORM?

❌

Without ORM

Developer writes SQL manually for every operation:

SQL
INSERT INTO STUDENT...
UPDATE STUDENT...
DELETE FROM STUDENT...
SELECT * FROM STUDENT...
✅

With ORM

Simply write one Java method:

Java
studentRepository.save(student);

ORM automatically generates the SQL.

What is Hibernate?

  • Hibernate is the most popular ORM framework for Java.
  • Spring ORM often works with Hibernate.
Spring Application
↓
Hibernate (ORM Framework)
↓
Database

MVC vs ORM — Quick Summary

ConceptFull FormWhat It Does
MVC Model-View-Controller Separates application into 3 layers for clean organization
ORM Object Relational Mapping Maps Java objects to database tables, auto-generates SQL
Hibernate — The most popular ORM framework for Java / Spring
Module 5 · Spring MVC & ORM · 5g · ii

MVC Configuration

Setting up Spring MVC so it knows which Controller handles which URL, and which View to display in response — the backbone of every Spring web application.

What is MVC Configuration?

MVC Configuration is the process of setting up Spring MVC so it can receive requests, process them, and return responses.

Why Do We Need Configuration?

Building a Website — Without Configuration
Without configuration, Spring doesn't know:

· Which Controller handles the request?
· Which View should be displayed?
· Which URL maps to which method?

So we configure Spring MVC to answer all these questions automatically.
❓

Without MVC Config

User sends request
↓
Spring doesn't know:
Which Controller?
Which View?
Which URL?

Application fails.

✅

With MVC Config

Spring knows:
Which class handles requests ✅
Which Controller to call ✅
Which View to display ✅
Where JSP/HTML pages are ✅

What MVC Configuration Answers

QuestionAnswered By
Which class handles requests?DispatcherServlet
Which Controller should be called?URL Mapping via @RequestMapping
Which View should be displayed?ViewResolver configuration
Where are the JSP/HTML pages?View prefix/suffix configuration
Where to scan Controllers?@ComponentScan

MVC Request Handling Flow

User sends HTTP Request (e.g. /home)
↓
DispatcherServlet receives the request
↓
Handler Mapping finds the correct Controller
↓
Controller processes the request & returns View name
↓
ViewResolver finds the correct View (JSP/HTML)
↓
Response returned to User

Advantages

Centralized request handling Easy URL mapping Clean architecture Automatic Controller discovery Easy View management
Module 5 · Spring MVC & ORM · 5g · iii

Controller Layer

The Controller is the entry point of every web request in Spring MVC — it receives the request, calls the service, and returns the view or response.

What is a Controller?

  • A Controller is a Spring MVC component that receives HTTP requests, processes them, communicates with the Model/Service layer, and returns a View or Response.
User visits: http://localhost:8080/student
The browser sends a request. Who receives it first?

Not the database. Not the Model.

The Controller receives it first (through the DispatcherServlet).

@Controller

@Controller tells Spring: "This class handles web requests."

Java — Syntax
@Controller
public class StudentController {

}

a) @RequestMapping

@RequestMapping maps a URL to a Controller or a specific method.

Class-Level Mapping

Java
@Controller
@RequestMapping("/student")
public class StudentController {

}

Now every request beginning with /student goes to this Controller.

Method-Level Mapping

Java
@RequestMapping("/list")
public String showStudents() {
    return "students";
}
ℹ️ Complete URL
/student/list

b) @GetMapping

Handles HTTP GET requests — used to view pages and retrieve data.

Java
@GetMapping("/students")
public String showStudents() {
    return "students";
}

When the browser requests GET /students, Spring calls this method.

c) @PostMapping

Handles HTTP POST requests — used to submit forms, save data, and insert records.

Java
@PostMapping("/save")
public String saveStudent() {
    return "success";
}

When a form is submitted: POST /save — this method executes.

Mapping Annotations — Summary

AnnotationHTTP MethodUsed For
@RequestMappingAnyGeneral URL mapping (class or method level)
@GetMappingGETView pages, retrieve data
@PostMappingPOSTSubmit forms, save/insert data
@PutMappingPUTUpdate existing records
@DeleteMappingDELETEDelete records

Complete Example

Java — StudentController.java
import org.springframework.stereotype.Controller;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;

@Controller  // Registers this class as a Controller
public class StudentController {

    // Handles GET request: /students
    @GetMapping("/students")
    public String showStudents() {
        // Returns the logical View name
        return "students";
    }
}

Advantages

Separates request handling from business logic Clean and organized architecture Easy URL management Supports REST and web applications Easy integration with Spring Boot
Module 5 · Spring MVC & ORM · 5g · iv

Model Layer

The Model carries data from the Controller to the View — the bridge that makes dynamic web pages possible in Spring MVC.

What is the Model Layer?

  • The Model Layer is responsible for holding and transferring data from the Controller to the View.

Why Do We Need the Model?

❌

Without Model

The View cannot access the data from the Controller.

The webpage would be empty.

✅

With Model

Data is added to the Model in the Controller.

The Model transfers the data to the View automatically.

Example Data
Suppose the Controller has:
Student Name = Vishal · Age = 20 · Branch = CSE

Without the Model, the View cannot see any of this. The Model is the delivery vehicle.

Spring Model Interface

Spring provides the Model interface to carry data from Controller to View.

Syntax

Java — Method Signature
public String home(Model model)

Adding Data to Model

Java
model.addAttribute("name", "Vishal");
ℹ️ How addAttribute Works
model.addAttribute("key", value)

The first argument is the key (used in the View to access the data).
The second argument is the value (the actual data to display).

Controller → Model → View Flow

Controller method runs
↓
model.addAttribute("name", "Vishal")
↓
Model holds the data
↓
Controller returns View name: "student"
↓
View accesses data from Model and renders the page

Complete Example

Java — StudentController.java
import org.springframework.stereotype.Controller;
import org.springframework.ui.Model;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;

@Controller
public class StudentController {

    @GetMapping("/student")
    public String showStudent(Model model) {

        // Add data to the Model
        model.addAttribute("name", "Vishal");
        model.addAttribute("branch", "CSE");

        // Return logical View name
        return "student";
    }
}
💡 What Happens
Spring passes the Model (with name="Vishal" and branch="CSE") to the student View. The View can then display: "Hello, Vishal — Branch: CSE".

Advantages

Clean separation between Controller and View Easy way to pass multiple data values Supports reusable Views Makes Controllers cleaner
Module 5 · Spring MVC & ORM · 5g · v

View Layer

The View Layer displays data to the user — turning raw data from the Model into a proper, formatted webpage.

What is the View Layer?

  • The View Layer is responsible for displaying data to the user.
  • It receives data from the Model and renders it as a webpage.
User searches for student details
↓
Controller gets the student information
↓
Model stores it
↓
View displays it as a webpage

Why Do We Need the View?

❌

Without a View

The browser cannot display information properly.

The user would only see raw data — no formatting, no layout.

✅

With a View

The same information appears as a proper webpage with formatting, headings, and layout.

View Technologies

Spring MVC supports many View technologies:

📄

a) JSP

Used in older Spring MVC applications.

Example: student.jsp

🌿

b) Thymeleaf

Used in modern Spring Boot applications.

Example: student.html

⚛️

c) HTML with Frameworks

HTML used with React, Angular, or Vue as a frontend framework communicating with Spring backend.

Complete Example — Controller + View

StudentController.java

Java
import org.springframework.stereotype.Controller;
import org.springframework.ui.Model;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;

@Controller
public class StudentController {

    @GetMapping("/student")
    public String showStudent(Model model) {
        // Add data to Model
        model.addAttribute("name", "Vishal");
        model.addAttribute("branch", "CSE");

        // Return View Name
        return "student";
    }
}

student.jsp (View)

JSP
Student Name : ${name}
Branch       : ${branch}
ℹ️ About ${name} Syntax
Don't worry about the ${name} syntax now. This is the JSP Expression Language (EL) which displays data from the Model. We'll study it in advanced topics. For now, just know that it displays data from the Model.
✅ Output
Student Details
Name : Vishal
Branch : CSE

MVC — Complete Layer Summary

LayerResponsibilityExample
Controller Receives HTTP request, calls Service, adds data to Model StudentController.java
Model Carries data from Controller to View model.addAttribute(...)
View Displays data to the user as a formatted page student.jsp / student.html

Advantages

Separates UI from business logic Easy to change webpage design Supports multiple View technologies Better code organization Reusable pages
Module 5 · Spring MVC & ORM · 5g · vi

Form Handling

Receiving user input from an HTML form, processing it in the Controller, and returning a response — the foundation of every interactive web page.

What is Form Handling?

Form Handling is the process of receiving user input from an HTML form, processing it in the Controller, and returning a response.

Student Registration Form
A student fills a registration form:
Name: Vishal · Age: 20 · Branch: CSE

After clicking Submit → data goes to the Spring Controller → Controller processes it and stores it.

This complete process is called Form Handling.

Why Do We Need Form Handling?

Every website needs user input. Examples:

Login Registration Contact Us Feedback Payment Booking Ticket
⚠️ Without Form Handling
Users cannot send data to the server. The application becomes completely static.

GET vs POST in Form Handling

👁️

a) GET Request — Display the Form

Used to show the form page to the user.

Java
@GetMapping("/register")
public String showForm() {
    return "register";
}
📤

b) POST Request — Submit the Form

Used to receive and process form data.

Java
@PostMapping("/register")
public String submitForm() {
    return "success";
}

GET vs POST — Comparison

FeatureGETPOST
PurposeDisplay the form pageSubmit form data to the server
Data visible in URL?✅ Yes (query params)❌ No (sent in request body)
Used forShowing pages, reading dataSaving data, inserting records
Spring annotation@GetMapping@PostMapping
Idempotent?✅ Yes (safe to repeat)❌ No (creates side effects)

Form Handling Flow

User visits GET /register → Form page displays
↓
User fills in the form and clicks Submit
↓
POST /register sent to Spring Controller
↓
Controller processes the data
↓
Controller returns success View
↓
Success page displayed to user

Advantages

Automatic form data binding Less boilerplate code Easy integration with Spring MVC Clean Controller methods Supports complex Java objects
Module 5 · Spring MVC & ORM · 5g · vii

Querying

Sending requests to the database to retrieve, insert, update, or delete data — and how Spring's Repository methods map to SQL operations.

What is a Query?

A Query is a request sent to the database to retrieve, insert, update, or delete data.

Student Database
Suppose your database contains:
IDNameBranch
1VishalCSE
2AmanIT
3RaviECE

If you want to display all students, Spring sends a query to the database. The database returns the data. This process is called Querying.

Types of Queries

🔖 1) Retrieve All Records
SQLSpring
SELECT * FROM Student;repository.findAll();
Returns: All Students
🔖 2) Retrieve One Record
SQLSpring
SELECT * FROM Student WHERE id = 1;repository.findById(1);
Returns: Student with ID = 1
✅ 3) Insert Data
SQLSpring
INSERT INTO Student ...repository.save(student);
✅ 4) Update Data
SQLSpring
UPDATE Student ...repository.save(student);
save() is used for both insert and update depending on whether the entity already exists.
⚠️ 5) Delete Data
SQLSpring
DELETE FROM Student WHERE id = 1;repository.deleteById(1);

SQL vs Spring Repository — Summary

OperationSQLSpring Repository Method
Read AllSELECT * FROM StudentfindAll()
Read OneSELECT * FROM Student WHERE id=1findById(1)
InsertINSERT INTO Student ...save(student)
UpdateUPDATE Student ...save(student)
DeleteDELETE FROM Student WHERE id=1deleteById(1)

Repository Interface Example

Java — StudentRepository
public interface StudentRepository {
    List<Student> findAll();
    Student findById(int id);
    void save(Student student);
    void deleteById(int id);
}
ℹ️ Note
In real Spring Data JPA, the repository usually extends JpaRepository. That topic is beyond the scope of this syllabus, so focus on understanding the methods conceptually.

Complete Example — Controller + Service

Controller

Java — StudentController.java
@Controller
public class StudentController {

    @GetMapping("/students")
    public String showStudents(Model model) {
        // Get data from Service
        List<Student> students = studentService.getAllStudents();
        // Add data to Model
        model.addAttribute("students", students);
        // Return View
        return "students";
    }
}

Service

Java — StudentService.java
public List<Student> getAllStudents() {
    return repository.findAll();
}
ℹ️ Output — Database Returns
IDNameBranch
1VishalCSE
2AmanIT

Advantages

Easy data retrieval Reduces manual database operations Clean architecture using Repository Easy integration with Spring ORM Improves code readability
Module 5 · Spring MVC & ORM · 5g · viii

Validation

Checking whether user input satisfies required rules before processing or storing it — protecting the application from bad data.

What is Validation?

Validation is the process of checking whether user input satisfies the required rules before processing or storing it.

Invalid Registration Form
Suppose a registration form asks for: Name · Email · Age.

User enters:
Name: ""  |  Email: abc  |  Age: -5

Should Spring save this? No.

Spring first validates the data. If invalid → error messages are shown. If valid → data is saved.

Real-Life Analogy — Exam Hall

Exam Invigilator
Before entering the exam hall, the invigilator checks:
Admit Card ✅ · ID Card ✅ · Signature ✅

If everything is correct → you enter. Otherwise → you are stopped.
Real LifeSpring MVC
StudentUser
InvigilatorValidation
Admit Card CheckValidation Rules
Exam HallDatabase

Common Validation Annotations

These are the annotations most commonly used in Spring (Jakarta Bean Validation).

AnnotationPurposeExample
@NotNullValue must not be nullName required
@NotBlankString must not be empty or whitespace" " rejected
@NotEmptyCollection/String must not be empty"" rejected
@Size(min, max)Checks string length rangeUsername 3–20 chars
@Min(value)Minimum numeric valueAge ≥ 18
@Max(value)Maximum numeric valueMarks ≤ 100
@EmailValid email formatabc@gmail.com
@PatternMatches a regular expressionPhone number format

Example — Student Class with Validation

Java — Student.java
import jakarta.validation.constraints.*;

public class Student {

    @NotBlank(message = "Name is required")
    private String name;

    @Email(message = "Invalid Email")
    private String email;

    @Min(value = 18, message = "Age must be at least 18")
    private int age;

    // Getters and Setters
}

Using @Valid in the Controller

@Valid tells Spring: "Validate this object before processing it."

Java — Controller
@PostMapping("/register")
public String saveStudent(
        @Valid @ModelAttribute Student student,
        BindingResult result) {

    if (result.hasErrors()) {
        // Validation failed — return form page
        return "register";
    }
    // Validation passed — save and show success
    return "success";
}

Validation Flow

User submits form
↓
@Valid triggers validation on the Student object
↓
BindingResult holds any validation errors
↓
If errors → return form with error messages
↓
If valid → save data and show success

Advantages

Prevents invalid data Improves application security Better user experience Easy integration with Spring MVC Reduces database errors
Module 5 · Spring MVC & ORM · 5g · ix

Exception Handling

Catching and handling runtime errors so the application stays alive and shows friendly error pages instead of crashing.

What is Exception Handling?

Exception Handling is the process of catching and handling runtime errors so that the application continues to work properly.

❌

Without Exception Handling

Java
int result = 10 / 0;
// Throws: ArithmeticException

Application → Crash 💥

✅

With Exception Handling

Application → Exception Handled → Friendly Error Page

Common Exceptions

ExceptionMeaning
ArithmeticExceptionDivide by zero
NullPointerExceptionUsing a null object
NumberFormatExceptionInvalid number conversion
FileNotFoundExceptionFile not found
SQLExceptionDatabase error

What is @ExceptionHandler?

  • @ExceptionHandler is used to handle specific exceptions inside a Controller.

Syntax

Java
@ExceptionHandler(ArithmeticException.class)
public String handleException() {
    return "error";
}

Complete Example

Java — StudentController.java
import org.springframework.stereotype.Controller;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.*;

@Controller
public class StudentController {

    @GetMapping("/divide")
    public String divide() {
        int result = 10 / 0;  // Exception occurs
        return "success";
    }

    // Handles ArithmeticException only for this Controller
    @ExceptionHandler(ArithmeticException.class)
    public String handleArithmeticException() {
        return "error";
    }
}

What is @ControllerAdvice?

Suppose you have: StudentController · EmployeeController · ProductController · LoginController. Do you write the same Exception Handler in every Controller? No.

Spring provides @ControllerAdvice — it creates one global exception handler for all Controllers.

Java — GlobalExceptionHandler.java
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ControllerAdvice;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ExceptionHandler;

@ControllerAdvice
public class GlobalExceptionHandler {

    @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class)
    public String handleException() {
        return "error";  // Returns error.jsp / error.html
    }
}

@ExceptionHandler vs @ControllerAdvice

Feature@ExceptionHandler@ControllerAdvice
ScopeInside one Controller onlyAll Controllers globally
TypeLocal exception handlingGlobal exception handling
ReusabilityLess reusableHighly reusable
Recommended forController-specific errorsApplication-wide errors

Advantages

Prevents application crashes Provides user-friendly error messages Centralized error handling Improves application reliability Better user experience
Module 5 · Spring Boot · 5h · i

Overview of Spring Boot

An extension of the Spring Framework that eliminates boilerplate configuration and lets you focus entirely on business logic — with embedded server, auto-configuration, and starter dependencies built in.

What is Spring Boot?

  • Spring Boot is an extension of the Spring Framework that makes it easier and faster to build Spring applications with minimum configuration.

The Problem Spring Boot Solves

Earlier, using only the Spring Framework, developers had to:

Configure XML files Configure DispatcherServlet Configure Tomcat Configure Beans Add many dependencies manually
✅ Spring Boot's Solution
Spring Boot automatically configures many things, allowing developers to focus mainly on business logic.

Real-Life Analogy — Smartphone

🔧

Traditional Spring

You buy a phone.

Then you manually install:
Operating System · Apps · Drivers · Settings

Everything manually.

📱

Spring Boot

You buy a phone.

Everything is already installed.

You simply switch it on and start using it.

Features of Spring Boot

🔖 1. Easy Setup
Very little configuration is required. Spring Boot auto-configures most things based on the libraries on the classpath.
🔖 2. Embedded Server
No need to install Tomcat separately. Spring Boot includes an embedded server:
Tomcat (Default) Jetty Undertow
🔖 3. Starter Dependencies
Instead of adding many individual libraries, Spring Boot provides Starters.

Example: spring-boot-starter-web — automatically includes all required web-related libraries.
🔖 4. Production Ready
Spring Boot provides production-ready features out of the box:
Health checks Monitoring Metrics
🔖 5. Rapid Development
Applications can be developed much faster compared to traditional Spring.

Traditional Spring vs Spring Boot

FeatureTraditional SpringSpring Boot
ConfigurationLots of XML / Java configAuto-configured
ServerInstall Tomcat manuallyEmbedded (built-in)
DependenciesAdd each library manuallyStarter bundles
Setup timeHoursMinutes
Boilerplate codeA lotMinimal
Production featuresManual setupBuilt-in

Advantages

Easy to learn Minimal configuration Faster development Embedded web server Starter dependencies Production-ready features Reduced boilerplate code
Module 5 · Spring Boot · 5h · ii

Simplifying Spring Configuration with Boot

How Spring Boot replaces XML files, manual dependency management, and Tomcat setup with annotations, starter bundles, and auto-configuration.

What Does Spring Boot Simplify?

Spring Boot simplifies Spring configuration by reducing manual configuration and allowing developers to build applications with minimal setup.

Traditional Spring vs Spring Boot — Student App

❌

Traditional Spring

Before writing even one Controller, you had to configure:

web.xml · DispatcherServlet · View Resolver · Bean Configuration · Tomcat · Dependencies

Lots of setup.

✅

Spring Boot

1. Create the project
2. Write the Controller
3. Run the application

Spring Boot configures everything automatically.

What Configuration Does Spring Boot Simplify?

🔖 1. XML Configuration → Annotations

Traditional Spring

XML
<bean id="student"

public class Student { }
No XML Bean configuration required.

pom.xml

Traditional Spring

Deploy WAR file.

No separate installation required.

Traditional Spring: Beans were declared in XML. Spring Boot: Beans are registered using annotations.

AreaTraditional SpringSpring Boot

Creating a Spring Boot Application

From Spring Initializr to a running application — the standard project structure, key files, and the @SpringBootApplication entry point.

What is a Spring Boot Application?

A Spring Boot Application is a Java application built using Spring Boot that can be started with very little configuration.

Creating a Spring Boot Project — Spring Initializr

Most developers create projects using Spring Initializr (start.spring.io). Provide:

FieldExample Value
Project TypeMaven
LanguageJava
Spring Boot Version3.x.x (latest)
Groupcom.demo
ArtifactStudentManagement

💡 Then download the project ZIP and open in your IDE.

Standard Folder Structure

Project Structure
StudentManagement/
│
├── src
│   ├── main
│   │     ├── java
│   │     │      └── DemoApplication.java      ← Main class
│   │     │
│   │     └── resources
│   │             ├── application.properties    ← Config file
│   │             ├── static                    ← CSS, JS, Images

Important Files

🔖 1. pom.xml — Maven Dependencies
Manages all Maven dependencies and controls the project build.
pom.xml — Example Dependency

Stores application configuration — port, database, app name, etc.

Module 5 · Spring Boot · 5h · iv

Auto-Configuration

Spring Boot automatically configures your application based on what libraries are on the classpath — write less, get more.

What is Auto-Configuration?

  • Auto-Configuration is a Spring Boot feature that automatically configures your application based on the libraries you have added as dependencies.
  • Spring Boot uses Auto-Configuration to reduce the manual configuration required by the developer.

Real-Life Analogy — Smart Home

Smart Home
Imagine a Smart Home. You don't manually switch on every device in the morning.

The Smart Home system detects:
· It's morning → Turn on lights
· Temperature is 30°C → Start AC
· It's time for coffee → Start coffee machine

Spring Boot Auto-Configuration works the same way.
Smart HomeSpring Boot
Smart Home SystemSpring Boot
Detects environmentDetects classpath libraries
Turns on devices automaticallyConfigures beans automatically
You just live in the houseYou just write business code

How Auto-Configuration Works

Developer adds a dependency (e.g. spring-boot-starter-web)
↓
Spring Boot scans the classpath
↓
Finds the library on the classpath
↓
Automatically configures related beans (DispatcherServlet · ViewResolver · Tomcat)
↓
Application is ready — developer writes business logic only

Auto-Configuration Examples

Dependency AddedAuto-Configured By Spring Boot
spring-boot-starter-webDispatcherServlet · Embedded Tomcat · ViewResolver
spring-boot-starter-data-jpaDataSource · EntityManager · Repositories
spring-boot-starter-securitySecurity filters · Login page · Authentication
spring-boot-starter-thymeleafThymeleaf template engine configuration

@EnableAutoConfiguration

This annotation tells Spring Boot to start Auto-Configuration. It is included inside @SpringBootApplication.

Java
@SpringBootApplication
// Internally includes:
// @Configuration + @ComponentScan + @EnableAutoConfiguration
public class DemoApplication {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(DemoApplication.class, args);
    }
}
ℹ️ How Spring Boot Knows What to Configure
Spring Boot reads configuration classes from spring.factories (or AutoConfiguration.imports in Spring Boot 3+). These files list all available Auto-Configuration classes. Spring Boot picks only the ones relevant to the current classpath.

Advantages

Zero XML configuration Automatic bean setup Saves development time Reduces human error Adapts to what's on the classpath Can be customized or disabled
Module 5 · Spring Boot · 5h · v

Convention over Configuration

A design philosophy where Spring Boot provides smart default settings so you only need to configure things when you want something different from the standard.

What is Convention over Configuration?

  • Convention over Configuration (CoC) is a design principle where the framework provides sensible default settings so developers don't have to specify everything.
  • Only when the developer wants something different from the default does he need to configure it.
ℹ️ Simple Formula
CoC = Sensible Defaults + Configure Only What You Need to Change

Real-Life Analogy — Mobile App

Mobile App Defaults
When you install a new mobile app (e.g. WhatsApp), it comes with default settings:

Language: English · Theme: Light · Notifications: On · Font Size: Medium

You don't configure everything from scratch. The app just works with defaults.

Only if you want something different — like Dark Mode — do you go to Settings and change it.

Spring Boot works exactly this way.

Spring Boot Conventions (Defaults)

What Spring Boot AssumesDefault Value
Server port8080
Application context path/
Web serverEmbedded Tomcat
View templates locationsrc/main/resources/templates/
Static resources locationsrc/main/resources/static/
Configuration fileapplication.properties

Overriding Convention

If you don't want the default port (8080), just override it in application.properties:

application.properties
# Override default port
server.port=9090

# Override app name
spring.application.name=StudentApp
💡 Key Insight
Spring Boot used port 8080 by default because of convention. You didn't need to configure anything. But when you needed port 9090, you configured it — that's overriding the convention.

Convention over Configuration vs Configuration over Convention

⚡

Convention over Configuration (CoC)

Spring Boot provides defaults.
Developer configures only what's different.
Less code, faster development.

🔧

Configuration over Convention

Developer configures everything manually.
Nothing assumed.
More control, more work.

Advantages

Reduces configuration work Faster project setup Cleaner and smaller codebase Beginners can get started quickly Sensible defaults prevent common mistakes Can always override when needed
Module 6 · Spring Data JPA · 6a

Introduction to Spring Data JPA

A Spring module that eliminates boilerplate database code — just define an interface and Spring automatically provides all CRUD operations.

What is JPA?

  • JPA (Java Persistence API) is a Java specification that defines how Java objects should be stored in a relational database.
  • JPA defines the rules. Hibernate implements those rules.
Electricity Example
JPA is like a standard electrical socket specification (rules for how sockets should work).

Hibernate is like a specific socket manufacturer that follows those rules and provides the actual product.

What is ORM (Recap)?

☕

Java World

Student student = new Student();

Works with objects.

🗄️

Database World

SELECT * FROM student;

Works with tables and rows.

ℹ️ ORM = The Bridge
ORM (Object Relational Mapping) automatically converts between Java objects and database rows. JPA is the ORM standard. Hibernate is the most popular ORM implementation.

What is Hibernate?

  • Hibernate is the most popular JPA implementation (ORM framework).
  • It automatically generates SQL queries from Java code.
  • Spring Boot uses Hibernate as the default JPA provider.
Spring Data JPA (High-level API)
↓
Hibernate (JPA Implementation)
↓
Database (MySQL / PostgreSQL / H2)

What is Spring Data JPA?

  • Spring Data JPA is a Spring module that makes it even easier to work with JPA and Hibernate.
  • It eliminates boilerplate code by automatically providing CRUD operations through Repository interfaces.
❌

Without Spring Data JPA

Java
// Manual EntityManager code
EntityManager em = ...;
TypedQuery<Student> q =
  em.createQuery("FROM Student",
     Student.class);
List<Student> list = q.getResultList();
✅

With Spring Data JPA

Java
// Just one line!
List<Student> list =
  repository.findAll();

Spring generates all the code automatically.

Key Concepts

ConceptWhat It IsExample
EntityA Java class mapped to a DB table@Entity class Student
RepositoryInterface for DB operationsJpaRepository
JPAJava Persistence API (specification)Rules/standard
HibernateJPA Implementation (ORM tool)Generates SQL
CRUDCreate · Read · Update · Deletesave · findAll · delete

Advantages

No boilerplate SQL code Auto-generated CRUD methods Easy database integration Works with any SQL database Reduces development time significantly Automatic schema creation

Setting Up a Spring Boot Project with Spring Data JPA

Configuring a Spring Boot application to communicate with a relational database — dependencies, application.properties, and Hibernate settings.

What is This Setup?

It is the process of configuring a Spring Boot application so that it can communicate with a relational database using Spring Data JPA — adding the required libraries and database configuration so the application can perform database operations.

Creating a Spring Boot Project

The application cannot establish a database connection. The MySQL driver is mandatory.

application.properties — Database Configuration

Location: src/main/resources/application.properties

application.properties — Database Config
# Database URL
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/employee_db

# Database Username
spring.datasource.username=root

# Database Password
spring.datasource.password=root

# JDBC Driver
spring.datasource.driver-class-name=com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver
PropertyPurpose
spring.datasource.urlDatabase location (host · port · DB name)
spring.datasource.usernameDatabase login username
spring.datasource.passwordDatabase login password
spring.datasource.driver-class-nameSpecifies the JDBC driver class

Hibernate Configuration

application.properties — Hibernate Config
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
spring.jpa.show-sql=true
spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.format_sql=true
PropertyDescription
ddl-auto=updateAutomatically updates DB tables on entity changes
show-sql=trueDisplays generated SQL in console
format_sql=trueFormats SQL output for readability

ddl-auto Values

ValueMeaning
noneNo schema changes made
validateValidates existing schema — no changes
updateUpdates tables without deleting existing data ✅ Most common
createDrops and recreates tables on startup
create-dropCreates on startup, drops on shutdown

Real-Life Analogy — Visiting a Friend

Real LifeSpring Boot
Friend's addressspring.datasource.url
Vehicle to travelMySQL JDBC Driver
Permission to enterUsername & Password

application.properties vs application.yml

📄

application.properties

Key-value format.
Easier for beginners.
Widely used in tutorials.

.properties
server.port=8080
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:mysql://...
📋

application.yml

YAML format (indented).
Cleaner for large projects.
Common in enterprise apps.

.yml
server:
  port: 8080
spring:
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:mysql://...
Module 6 · Spring Data JPA · 6c

Entity Mapping

The process of connecting Java classes to database tables using JPA annotations — telling Hibernate which class is a table, which field is the primary key, and how each variable maps to a column.

What is Entity Mapping?

  • Entity Mapping is the process of connecting a Java Class with a Database Table using annotations.
  • It tells JPA: which class represents a table · which variables represent columns · which field is the primary key · how objects should be stored.
Different Languages
A database understands: Tables · Rows · Columns
Java understands: Classes · Objects · Variables

They speak different "languages." Entity Mapping acts as the translator between them.

What is an Entity?

  • An Entity is a Java class that represents a table in the database.
  • Each object of the entity represents one row of the table.
🗄️

Database Table

Employee_IDNameSalary
101Rahul50000
102Amit60000
☕

Java Entity

Employee employee = new Employee();

One object = One row

Important JPA Annotations — Overview

AnnotationPurpose
@EntityMarks a class as a JPA Entity
@TableMaps entity to a specific table name
@IdDeclares the Primary Key field
@GeneratedValueAuto-generates the Primary Key value
@ColumnMaps a field to a specific column
@TransientField is NOT stored in the database
@TemporalMaps Date/Time types (legacy — java.util.Date)
@EnumeratedStores Java Enum values in DB

1) @Entity

Marks a class as a JPA Entity. Every Entity class must have this annotation.

Java
@Entity
public class Employee {
    // ...
}

2) @Table

Maps the entity to a specific table name. If not specified, the class name is used as the table name.

Java
@Entity
@Table(name = "emp")
public class Employee {
    // Table name in DB: "emp" not "Employee"
}

3) @Id — Primary Key

Every Entity must have one @Id field. It represents the unique identifier for each row.

Java
@Entity
public class Employee {
    @Id
    private Long id;
}
ℹ️ Primary Key Properties
Unique · Cannot be NULL · Identifies one record · Only one per table (simple key)

4) @GeneratedValue

Specifies how the primary key value is auto-generated.

StrategyMeaning
AUTOLet the persistence provider decide
IDENTITYDatabase handles auto-increment ✅ Most common
SEQUENCEUses a database sequence
TABLEUses a separate table to track IDs
Java
@Id
@GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
private Long id;

5) @Column

Maps a field to a specific column. Useful when the field name differs from the column name.

Java
@Column(name = "employee_name")
private String name;

@Column(name = "salary")
private Double salary;
AttributePurpose
nameColumn name in DB
nullableAllow NULL values or not
uniqueEnforce uniqueness
lengthMaximum string length
updatableWhether the column can be updated

6) @Transient

The field will be ignored during DB operations — not stored, not retrieved. Useful for temporary or calculated fields.

Java
@Transient
private String tempData;  // Not saved to DB

7) @Temporal (Legacy)

Used with java.util.Date to specify how date/time is stored.

Java
@Temporal(TemporalType.DATE)
private Date birthDate;  // Stores DATE only

// TemporalType.DATE      → Date only
// TemporalType.TIME      → Time only
// TemporalType.TIMESTAMP → Date + Time

8) @Enumerated

Stores Java Enum values in the database — as index (ORDINAL) or name (STRING).

Java
public enum Status { ACTIVE, INACTIVE, PENDING }

@Enumerated(EnumType.STRING)
private Status status;  // Stores "ACTIVE" not 0
💡 Always use EnumType.STRING
ORDINAL stores 0/1/2 — if you reorder the enum, all existing data becomes wrong. STRING stores the name, which is safe.

Quick Comparisons

@Entity vs @Table

@Entity@Table
Declares JPA EntityMaps to table name
MandatoryOptional

@Transient vs @Column

@Transient@Column
NOT stored in DBStored in DB
Temporary fieldPersistent field
Module 6 · Spring Data JPA · 6d

Spring Data Repositories

The bridge between your application and database — define an interface that extends JpaRepository and Spring automatically provides all CRUD, pagination, sorting, and custom query operations.

What is a Repository?

  • A Repository is a Java interface that acts as a bridge between the Application and the Database.
  • It is responsible for: Save · Update · Delete · Find · Search — all without writing SQL.
  • Repository = Data Access Layer (DAL) that performs CRUD operations on the database.

Why Do We Need Repositories?

❌

Before Spring Data JPA (DAO)

Developers wrote DAO classes containing:
SQL Queries · JDBC Code · Connection Handling · ResultSet Mapping

Problems: Large code · Difficult maintenance · Duplicate logic · Time consuming

✅

With Spring Data JPA Repositories

Just define an interface.
Spring automatically provides all ready-made database operations.

No implementation needed.

Types of Spring Data Repositories

Repository — Root / Marker interface
↓ extends
CrudRepository — Basic CRUD (save · find · delete · count)
↓ extends
PagingAndSortingRepository — Adds Pagination + Sorting
↓ extends
⭐ JpaRepository — CRUD + Pagination + Sorting + Batch + Flush
RepositoryWhat It ProvidesWhen to Use
RepositoryMarker only — no methodsRarely used directly
CrudRepositoryBasic CRUD operationsSimple apps
PagingAndSortingRepositoryCRUD + Pagination + SortingList views with pages
JpaRepository ⭐Everything above + Batch + FlushMost applications

Creating a Repository

Java — EmployeeRepository.java
public interface EmployeeRepository
        extends JpaRepository<Employee, Integer> {

}
KeywordPurpose
interfaceRepository is an interface — no implementation needed
extends JpaRepositoryInherits all ready-made database methods
EmployeeThe Entity class this repository manages
IntegerData type of the Primary Key

What Does JpaRepository Provide?

Without writing any code, you automatically get:

MethodPurpose
save(entity)Insert or Update a record
findById(id)Find record by Primary Key
findAll()Retrieve all records
deleteById(id)Delete a record by Primary Key
count()Count total records
existsById(id)Check if a record exists
💡 No Implementation Required
Spring automatically generates the implementation at runtime. You only define the interface.

Derived Query Methods

Spring Data JPA can automatically generate SQL from method names. This is called Query Method Derivation.

Java — Example
// Method name:
List<Employee> findByName(String name);

// Spring auto-generates:
// SELECT * FROM Employee WHERE name = ?

Common Derived Query Keywords

Method PrefixSQL Meaning
findBySELECT WHERE
existsByCheck existence
countByCOUNT WHERE
deleteByDELETE WHERE
findFirstByFirst matching record
findTopByTop matching record

Conditions Supported

KeywordSQL Equivalent
AndAND
OrOR
BetweenBETWEEN
LessThan / GreaterThan< / >
Like / ContainingLIKE '%value%'
StartingWith / EndingWithLIKE 'value%' / LIKE '%value'
OrderByORDER BY
Java — findByNameAndSalary Example
List<Employee> findByNameAndSalary(String name, Double salary);

// Auto-generates:
// SELECT * FROM Employee WHERE name=? AND salary=?

@Query — Custom JPQL

When method names become too long or the query is too complex, use @Query to write custom JPQL directly.

Java
@Query("SELECT e FROM Employee e")
List<Employee> getAllEmployees();
FeatureDerived Query@Query
How it worksAuto from method nameDeveloper writes JPQL
Query complexitySimpleComplex
FlexibilityLess flexibleMore flexible
Code amountLess codeMore control

What is JPQL?

JPQL (Java Persistence Query Language) is the query language used by JPA. It works with Entity names and fields, not table names and column names.

🗄️

SQL

SQL
SELECT *
FROM employee

Uses table name: employee

☕

JPQL

JPQL
SELECT e
FROM Employee e

Uses Entity name: Employee

Module 6 · Spring Data JPA · 6e

CRUD Operations with Spring Data JPA

Create · Read · Update · Delete — the four fundamental database operations, and how Spring Data JPA provides them all through a single Repository interface.

What is CRUD?

LetterFull FormPurposeSQL
CCreateInsert new dataINSERT
RReadRetrieve existing dataSELECT
UUpdateModify existing dataUPDATE
DDeleteRemove existing dataDELETE
ℹ️ Universal Pattern
Almost every application — Banking · E-Commerce · Hospital · Social Media — performs these four operations on data.

Real-Life Analogy — ATM

CRUDATM Example
CreateOpen a new account
ReadCheck balance
UpdateChange mobile number
DeleteClose account

C — Create Operation

The Create operation inserts a new record into the database. Spring Data JPA provides save(entity).

Java
Employee emp = new Employee();
emp.setName("Rahul");
emp.setSalary(50000.0);

employeeRepository.save(emp);
// Generates: INSERT INTO employee ...

R — Read Operations

Read operations retrieve data from the database.

MethodPurposeEquivalent SQL
findAll()Retrieve all recordsSELECT * FROM employee
findById(id)Retrieve one record by PKSELECT * FROM employee WHERE id=?
existsById(id)Check if record existsSELECT EXISTS(...)
count()Count total recordsSELECT COUNT(*) FROM employee
Java — Read Examples
// Get all employees
List<Employee> all = employeeRepository.findAll();

// Get employee by ID
Optional<Employee> emp = employeeRepository.findById(101);

// Count
long total = employeeRepository.count();
🔖 What is Optional?
findById() returns an Optional<Employee> — not null.

Why? Sometimes the requested record doesn't exist. Instead of returning null (which causes NullPointerException), Spring returns an Optional so the developer handles the missing case safely.

U — Update Operation

Spring Data JPA uses the same save() method for both Insert and Update.

Call save(entity)
↓
Does the Primary Key already exist in DB?
↓
Yes → UPDATE
No → INSERT
Java — Update Example
Optional<Employee> opt = employeeRepository.findById(101);
if (opt.isPresent()) {
    Employee emp = opt.get();
    emp.setSalary(70000.0);
    employeeRepository.save(emp);  // UPDATE (ID exists)
}

D — Delete Operations

MethodPurposeEquivalent SQL
delete(entity)Delete an entity objectDELETE FROM employee WHERE id=?
deleteById(id)Delete using Primary KeyDELETE FROM employee WHERE id=?
deleteAll()Delete all recordsDELETE FROM employee
Java — Delete Example
employeeRepository.deleteById(101);
// Generates: DELETE FROM employee WHERE id=101

All JpaRepository CRUD Methods

MethodOperationReturn TypePurpose
save(entity)Create / UpdateEntityInsert or Update one record
saveAll(list)Create / UpdateListSave multiple records at once
findAll()ReadListRetrieve all records
findById(id)ReadOptionalRetrieve by Primary Key
existsById(id)ReadbooleanCheck if record exists
count()ReadlongCount total records
delete(entity)DeletevoidDelete an entity object
deleteById(id)DeletevoidDelete by Primary Key
deleteAll()DeletevoidDelete all records
Module 6 · Spring Data JPA · 6f

Query Methods and Named Queries

Let your method names do the SQL writing — Spring Data JPA reads the method name and auto-generates the query. For reusable complex queries, define them once with @NamedQuery.

What are Query Methods?

  • A Query Method is a repository method whose name itself tells Spring Data JPA what query to generate.
  • Spring reads the method name and creates the required database query automatically.
❌

Traditional Approach

SQL
SELECT * FROM employee
WHERE name = 'Rahul';

Written manually every time.

✅

Spring Data JPA

Java
findByName(String name);

Spring auto-generates the SQL.

Query Method Naming Convention

Pattern
Prefix + By + FieldName + Condition

Example:  findByName
          ├── find  → what to do (retrieve)
          ├── By    → connector keyword
          └── Name  → field to filter on

Common Query Method Prefixes

PrefixPurposeExample
findByRetrieve datafindByName()
readByRetrieve datareadByEmail()
getByRetrieve one or more recordsgetByDepartment()
existsByCheck existenceexistsByEmail()
countByCount recordscountByDepartment()
deleteByDelete recordsdeleteByName()

Keywords in Query Methods

KeywordSQL EquivalentExample
AndANDfindByNameAndSalary()
OrORfindByNameOrDepartment()
BetweenBETWEENfindBySalaryBetween()
LessThan / GreaterThan< / >findByAgeLessThan()
LikeLIKEfindByNameLike()
ContainingLIKE %value%findByNameContaining()
StartingWithLIKE value%findByNameStartingWith()
EndingWithLIKE %valuefindByNameEndingWith()
OrderByORDER BYfindByAgeOrderByNameAsc()
InINfindByDepartmentIn()
NotNOTfindByNameNot()
IsNull / IsNotNullIS NULL / IS NOT NULLfindByEmailIsNull()
True / False= TRUE / = FALSEfindByActiveTrue()

Common Query Methods — Quick Reference

Query MethodGenerated SQL (Conceptually)
findByName(name)WHERE name = ?
findByDepartment(dept)WHERE department = ?
findByAgeGreaterThan(age)WHERE age > ?
findBySalaryBetween(a, b)WHERE salary BETWEEN ? AND ?
findByNameContaining(s)WHERE name LIKE '%s%'
findByNameStartingWith(s)WHERE name LIKE 's%'
findByNameEndingWith(s)WHERE name LIKE '%s'

What are Named Queries?

  • A Named Query is a query that is defined once with a name and can be reused multiple times across the application.
  • Instead of writing the same query repeatedly, define it once on the Entity class.
Reusability Easy maintenance Centralized query definition

@NamedQuery — Single Named Query

Java — Entity with @NamedQuery
@Entity
@NamedQuery(
    name  = "Employee.findByDept",
    query = "SELECT e FROM Employee e WHERE e.department = :dept"
)
public class Employee {
    // ...
}
ElementPurpose
nameUnique query identifier used to call it later
queryThe JPQL query to execute

@NamedQueries — Multiple Named Queries

When an entity needs multiple Named Queries, group them inside @NamedQueries.

Java
@Entity
@NamedQueries({
    @NamedQuery(name = "Employee.findAll",
                query = "SELECT e FROM Employee e"),
    @NamedQuery(name = "Employee.findByDept",
                query = "SELECT e FROM Employee e WHERE e.department = :dept")
})
public class Employee { }

What are Dynamic Queries?

  • A Dynamic Query is a query whose search conditions change at runtime based on user input.
  • Different combinations of filters may be applied each time the query runs.
Amazon Search — Dynamic Query Example
Sometimes you search by: Brand
Sometimes by: Price
Sometimes by: Rating
Sometimes by all three combined.

The query changes depending on which filters are applied — that is a Dynamic Query.
Query TypeWhen to UseHow
Derived QuerySimple, fixed conditionsMethod name convention
@QueryComplex fixed JPQLWrite JPQL manually
@NamedQueryReusable fixed queriesDefine on Entity class
Dynamic QueryConditions change at runtimeJPA Criteria API / Specification
Module 6 · Spring Data JPA · 6g

Auditing with Spring Data JPA

Automatically tracking who created a record, who modified it, and when — without writing a single line of tracking code manually.

What is Auditing?

  • Auditing is the process of automatically recording who created, who modified, when it was created, and when it was last modified for a database record.
  • Auditing = Tracking the history of database records automatically.
ℹ️ Auditing Answers
Who created this record? · When was it created? · Who modified it? · When was it last modified?

Why Do We Need Auditing?

Employee Salary Change
An employee's salary changes from ₹50,000 to ₹70,000.

Later, the manager asks: "Who changed the salary? When was it changed?"

Without auditing → No record of the change.
With auditing → System automatically stores this information.

Real-Life Example — Google Docs

Shared Google Document
When you edit a shared document, it shows:

Created By: Vishal    Created On: 15 July 2026
Last Modified By: Rahul    Last Modified On: 18 July 2026

This is Auditing.

Entity Auditing

Auditing adds tracking columns directly to the database table alongside normal data:

IDNameCreated ByCreated DateLast Modified ByLast Modified Date
1RahulAdmin10-JulManager15-Jul

The 4 Auditing Annotations

🔖 @CreatedBy
Automatically stores who created the record. Set once at creation — never updated.

Java
@CreatedBy
private String createdBy;
Useful for: Banking · Hospital Systems · ERP · Inventory — where knowing the creator is important.
🔖 @LastModifiedBy
Automatically stores who last modified the record. Updated after each modification.

Java
@LastModifiedBy
private String lastModifiedBy;
Useful for: Audit Trails · Compliance · Accountability.
🔖 @CreatedDate
Automatically stores when the record was created. Set once — never updated.

Java
@CreatedDate
private LocalDateTime createdDate;
Useful for: Time-based reports · Analytics · Historical tracking · Registration Date.
🔖 @LastModifiedDate
Automatically stores when the record was last modified. Updated after each modification.

Java
@LastModifiedDate
private LocalDateTime lastModifiedDate;
Useful for: Audit trails · Change logs · Data freshness tracking.

Auditing Annotations — Summary

AnnotationStoresWhen Updated
@CreatedByWho created the recordSet once at creation
@LastModifiedByWho last modified the recordUpdated on every modification
@CreatedDateWhen the record was createdSet once at creation
@LastModifiedDateWhen the record was last modifiedUpdated on every modification

Complete Audited Entity Example

Java — Employee.java (with Auditing)
@Entity
@EntityListeners(AuditingEntityListener.class)
public class Employee {

    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    private String name;

    // ── Audit Fields ──
    @CreatedBy
    private String createdBy;

    @LastModifiedBy
    private String lastModifiedBy;

    @CreatedDate
    private LocalDateTime createdDate;

    @LastModifiedDate
    private LocalDateTime lastModifiedDate;
}

Configuring Auditing

Spring Data JPA Auditing is not enabled by default. It must be enabled explicitly.

Java — Main Application
@SpringBootApplication
@EnableJpaAuditing  // ← Enable auditing
public class DemoApplication {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(DemoApplication.class, args);
    }
}
ℹ️ Configuration Steps
1. Add @EnableJpaAuditing to the main class.
2. Add @EntityListeners(AuditingEntityListener.class) to the Entity.
3. Provide an AuditorAware bean to supply the current user for @CreatedBy and @LastModifiedBy.

Advantages

Automatically tracks record history Improves accountability Helps in debugging Useful for compliance and security Reduces manual tracking code Essential for enterprise applications
Module 6 · Spring Data JPA · 6h

Spring Data JPA Projections

Fetch only the columns you need — not the entire entity. Projections reduce database load, memory usage, and improve performance by returning targeted subsets of data.

What are Projections?

  • A Projection is a technique used to retrieve only the required fields from the database instead of fetching the complete Entity.
❌

Without Projection

IDNameSalaryDeptEmail
101Rahul50000ITrahul@gmail.com

All 5 columns fetched — even unused ones.

✅

With Projection

NameDept
RahulIT

Only the 2 required columns fetched.

Real-Life Analogy — Aadhaar Card

College Registration
Your Aadhaar Card contains: Name · DOB · Address · Mobile · Aadhaar Number.

When registering for a college, the college only asks for: Name · Address.

You don't submit every detail. That is exactly what a Projection does.

Types of Projections

🔌

Interface-Based Projection

Define a Java Interface with getter methods for required fields. Spring automatically implements it.

Best for: Simple, read-only data.

📦

Class-Based Projection (DTO)

Define a DTO class with a constructor matching the required fields.

Best for: Complex data, computed fields, reuse across services.

Interface-Based Projection

Create an interface with getter methods for only the fields you need:

Java — EmployeeView.java (Interface Projection)
public interface EmployeeView {
    String getName();
    String getDepartment();
}
Java — Repository using Interface Projection
List<EmployeeView> findByDepartment(String department);
💡 Spring Auto-Implements
You don't write the implementation. Spring Data JPA automatically generates it at runtime — only fetching name and department from the database.

Class-Based Projection (DTO)

Create a DTO class with a constructor matching the projected fields:

Java — EmployeeDTO.java
public class EmployeeDTO {
    private String name;
    private String department;

    public EmployeeDTO(String name, String department) {
        this.name = name;
        this.department = department;
    }
    // Getters...
}
Java — @Query with Constructor Expression
@Query("SELECT new com.example.EmployeeDTO(e.name, e.department) FROM Employee e")
List<EmployeeDTO> findEmployeeDetails();

Constructor Expressions

A Constructor Expression creates a DTO directly from the query result — no complete Entity is created.

JPQL query runs: SELECT new EmployeeDTO(e.name, e.salary)
↓
Spring calls EmployeeDTO(name, salary) constructor directly
↓
DTO object returned — no full Employee entity in memory
Less memory Faster execution Better performance Clean architecture

@Value in Projections

@Value allows creating calculated or combined values inside an Interface Projection using Spring Expression Language (SpEL).

Java — Combining firstName + lastName
public interface EmployeeView {

    @Value("#{target.firstName + ' ' + target.lastName}")
    String getFullName();  // Returns "Rahul Sharma"
}
ℹ️ When to Use @Value
When the data you need isn't stored directly — e.g. combining firstName + lastName into a full name, or computing a value from existing fields.

Interface vs Class Projection

FeatureInterface ProjectionClass (DTO) Projection
DefinitionJava interface with gettersJava class with constructor
ImplementationAuto by SpringDeveloper writes
Computed fieldsVia @ValueIn constructor / methods
ComplexitySimpleMore control
Best forSimple read-only dataComplex transformations

Advantages

Retrieves only required data Improves application performance Reduces memory consumption Reduces database load Faster query execution Cleaner API responses Better scalability

Spring Data JPA and Spring Boot Integration

How Spring Boot auto-configures Hibernate, DataSource, EntityManager, and Repositories from just two dependencies and a few lines in application.properties — and how to scale to multiple databases.

What is Spring Data JPA + Spring Boot Integration?

  • Integration means Spring Boot automatically configures Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, and the Database Connection with minimal manual setup.
  • Instead of manually configuring dozens of classes, Spring Boot does it automatically.

Before Spring Boot vs With Spring Boot

❌

Before Spring Boot

Developers manually configured:

DataSource · Hibernate · EntityManager · Transaction Manager · Repository Scanner · Database Driver

All manually. Hundreds of lines.

✅

With Spring Boot

Add Dependencies
↓
Configure application.properties
↓
Run Application ✅

Spring Boot configures everything else.

What is Auto-Configuration?

Auto-Configuration is Spring Boot's ability to automatically configure beans based on the dependencies present in the project.

🔖 Example
When your project contains spring-boot-starter-data-jpa + MySQL Driver, Spring Boot automatically configures:

DataSource Hibernate EntityManager Transaction Manager Repository Beans

Without writing a single configuration class.

What is a DataSource?

  • A DataSource is an object responsible for establishing and managing connections to the database.
  • DataSource = A connection provider between the application and the database.
  • Without a DataSource, the application cannot communicate with the database.
Spring Boot Application
↓
DataSource (Connection Provider)
↓
Database (MySQL / PostgreSQL / Oracle)

Externalizing Configuration

Externalizing Configuration means keeping configuration values outside the Java code — in application.properties or application.yml.

❌

Without External Config

Open Java Code → Modify Password → Compile Again

Any config change requires recompilation.

✅

With External Config

Open application.properties → Change Password → Restart

Much easier. No recompilation.

application.properties — Common Properties

application.properties
# Database
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/employee_db
spring.datasource.username=root
spring.datasource.password=root
spring.datasource.driver-class-name=com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver

# Hibernate

PropertyPurpose

Managing Multiple Data Sources

Spring Boot supports connecting to more than one database simultaneously — useful in large enterprise applications that separate data by domain.

Company Department Analogy
Instead of keeping everything in one room, a company has separate departments:
HR Department · Finance Department · Sales Department

Similarly, an application can use multiple databases:
MySQL (Employee Data) · Oracle (Payroll) · PostgreSQL (Inventory)
application.properties — Multiple DataSources
# Primary DataSource (Employee DB)
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/employee_db
spring.datasource.username=root
spring.datasource.password=root

# Secondary DataSource (Inventory DB)
inventory.datasource.url=jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/inventory_db
inventory.datasource.username=root
inventory.datasource.password=root
AdvantageDescription
Better scalabilityEach database can scale independently
